::: {#rem-expectation-long-run-average}
#### The expectation is the long-run average of repeated draws

The [weak law of large numbers](#thm-wlln) gives the expectation a second reading.
Draw $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ independently from the distribution of $X$,
so that they are [IID](independence.qmd#def-iid) with population mean $\E{X}$.
The sample mean of the first $n$ draws then
[converges in probability](#def-convergence-in-probability) to $\E{X}$:
for a large $n$, the average of the draws is very probably close to $\E{X}$.
So the expectation is the value that the average of many repeated draws settles near.

For a finite population, the two readings agree.
As [the population-mean proposition](expectation.qmd#prp-population-mean-expectation) shows, $\E{X}$ is the average over the whole population
when $X$ is the value of one unit [chosen at random](probability-basics.qmd#def-random-choice).
Units drawn at random with replacement are IID,
so the average over many draws settles near that population average.

:::
